title: Nightlife
theme: The club, a bar regular, a night out going wrong, a turn away at the door, a late walk home.

storylets.title: Forty people and a rope
storylets.note: Friends waiting outside the club. Common, cheap, loud.

A.desc: an adult in the rope line

b1: {A} and {B.desc} join the rope line, twenty back from the door.
{A} and {B.desc} take a spot at the rope. The line shuffles.
{A} and {B.desc} fall in behind a tall figure in a neon jacket.
{B.desc} drags {A} to the end of the rope and crosses both arms.
b2: {A} and {B.desc} talk over the thump from inside, heads close.
{B.desc} shows {A} something on a handset and they both laugh.
{A} jokes with {B.desc} and swaps a cup of something warm.
{B.desc} bounces on the balls of {B.his} feet and chatters.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "{B.first}, stop bouncing, we are not that late."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "If I am not in by ten, {A.nick}, I swear."

storylets.title: The bouncer's nod
storylets.note: A regular is waved through. Shows regular:club without naming anyone.

b1: {A} arrives at the end of the rope and is already looking at the door.
{A} approaches the rope with a casual stride and a half wave.
{A} comes up to the club, collar high, eyes on the bouncers.
{A} strolls up the walk, hands in pockets.
b2: A bouncer unhooks the rope for {A} with a nod. {A} goes in without breaking stride.
The door staff wave {A} in. Others in line grumble.
{A} is admitted at once. The door closes on the bass.
A bouncer jerks a thumb. {A} slips through.

log: {A} was waved straight past the line. The door staff did not ask for anything.
{A} is a known face at this door.

storylets.title: Not tonight
storylets.note: Turned away at the rope. A friend walks off with them. Chain: ngt.makes-it-in-later, or it ends there.

b1: A bouncer stops {A} at the rope with one flat hand. {A} is turned away.
{A} reaches the front and is refused entry. A short exchange; the rope stays closed.
{A} is shoved back a step by a bouncer and told to move on.
b2: {B.desc} catches up with {A} and talks fast, a hand on {A}'s sleeve.
{A} says something and {B.desc} answers with a flat laugh.
{B.desc} points down the block and tries a smile.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} walk off into the dark, {B.desc} talking the whole way.
{A} lets {B.desc} steer away from the door. Neither looks back.
The two of them head down the street side by side.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "Third time this month. Same guy on the door, same excuse."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Forget it. We can try the lawn bar instead."

storylets.title: The same door, a better night

b1: {A} comes up to the rope for the second time this week, jacket straightened.
{A} arrives and tugs at a sleeve. The line is shorter tonight.
{A} walks to the rope with careful steps.
b2: The bouncer looks {A} over, then lifts the rope. {A} goes in, quick.
{A} is admitted. A small fist pump on the way through the door.
The door staff let {A} in without a word.

storylets.title: Dancing on the sidewalk
storylets.note: Someone spills out of the club still dancing. Visible, joyful, harmless.

b1: {A} comes out of the club door in a rush of bass and steam.
{A} leaves the club, jacket over a shoulder, grinning.
{A} emerges from the club door and blinks at the street.
b2: {A} dances along the sidewalk to music no one else can hear.
{A} spins once on the curb and keeps moving to a private beat.
{A} dances a few steps, nearly bumps a lamp post, and bows to it.

storylets.title: One drink too many
storylets.note: Throw-up outside a club, a friend holding a jacket. Plain, unglamorous, true.

A.desc: an adult who has had too much

b1: {A} comes out of the club door fast, hand over the mouth.
{A} stumbles out of the door and heads for the curb.
{A} leaves the club at speed, one hand on the wall.
b2: {A} bends over the gutter and is sick.
{A} retches at the curb. A puddle spreads.
{A} throws up beside a drain, hands on knees.
b3: {B.desc} pats {A}'s back, hands over a cup of water, and steers {A} away.
{B.desc} takes {A}'s arm and the two shuffle off together.
{B.desc} drapes a jacket over {A} and walks {A} toward the metro.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Next time I count your drinks, friend. Three, not five."
Overheard: {A} says: "Sorry. You are a good friend. Don't tell anyone."

storylets.title: Escorted to the curb
storylets.note: Bouncers walk someone out. Chain: ngt.cooling-off-walk fizzle only.

b1: Two bouncers walk {A} out of the club door, one on each arm.
{A} is ejected from the club and set down on the sidewalk.
Door staff escort {A} off the step and release {A.his} sleeves.
b2: {A} stands on the sidewalk and straightens a collar with great dignity.
{A} stays at the curb, arms spread, saying something to the door.
{A} lingers, then points at the club and shouts.
b3: {A} walks off down the block, muttering.
{A} heads for the metro at a stiff pace.
{A} turns and wanders away, hands in pockets.

log: Overheard: {A} shouts: "I will be back! I will be back, and I will be wearing a better jacket!"
Overheard: {A} says to the air: "Not even a refund on the drink."

storylets.title: The bar kiosk, round two
storylets.note: A kiosk drink. The keeper knows the order.

b1: {A} steps up to the kiosk and orders two fingers of something amber.
{A} leans on the counter and says the usual without looking up.
{A} reaches the kiosk and holds up a coin.
{A} gets to the window and points at a bottle.
b2: {B.desc} slides a glass across without a word.
{B.desc} serves {A} and wipes a ring from the counter.
{B.desc} pours it slowly and sets it down.
{B.desc} serves up the drink and taps the till.
b3: {A} drinks standing, one elbow on the counter.
{A} takes a long sip and watches the club door.
{A} sips and looks up at the sign.
{A} finishes the glass in three swallows.

log: {A} ordered without being asked what; the server already knew.

storylets.title: The long way back
storylets.note: A solitary walk home late. Atmospheric, no event.

b1: {A} walks alone down the block, hood up, under dripping neon.
{A} heads along the empty sidewalk, hands deep in pockets.
{A} takes the long way past the shuttered stalls.
{A} walks the middle of the street, boots echoing.
b2: {A} stops under a lamp and looks up at the buildings.
{A} stays at a crossing and waits for a light that does not change.
{A} stands at the corner and rubs both arms.
{A} lingers by the fountain for a moment.
b3: {A} climbs the step and goes in. The door slides shut.
{A} reaches the door and enters.
{A} steps inside and the light behind the panel goes on.
{A} arrives at the home door and goes in.

log: {A} lives at this door; it opened to {A.him} at once.
{A} came home to this address late at night.

storylets.title: The doorman's shift begins
storylets.note: A club worker arrives early. Routine seen from the other side of the rope.

b1: {A} comes down the block in a dark uniform, a thermos under one arm.
{A} walks up with a clipboard and an unlit sign under one arm.
{A} crosses to the club in a long coat, badge swinging.
{A} arrives early, rolling both shoulders.
b2: {A} unlocks the staff side and goes in.
{A} swipes a badge at the club door and enters.
{A} slips in through the side door, still yawning.
{A} enters through the club door and it closes.

log: The badge reads Door Staff, Neon Dome.
A uniform patch reads Neon Dome, Security.

storylets.title: Picked up at the drop-off
storylets.note: Two people leave together by car. Observed only. Fits the ambiguity theme but leaves it as texture.

b1: {A} stands at the drop-off with hands in pockets and the neon behind.
{A} lingers at the lift base, glancing at the sky.
{A} waits near the drop-off sign.
b2: {B.desc} walks up and stops beside {A}.
{B.desc} crosses the plaza to {A} and says a few words.
{B.desc} approaches the drop-off at a brisk pace.
b3: A car drops to the pad. Both get in. It rises.
{A} and {B.desc} climb in together and the car lifts away.
The pair board a waiting car and ride up out of sight.

storylets.title: One shoulder under another
storylets.note: A friend helps someone home. Shows friend relation by action, never by label.

b1: {B.desc} takes most of {A}'s weight and steers down the block.
{A} leans heavily on {B.desc} all the way along the wall.
{B.desc} half carries {A} past the closed stalls.
b2: They stop at a bench. {A} sits with eyes shut, {B.desc} standing guard.
{B.desc} lowers {A} onto a bench and hands over water.
{A} slumps on the bench while {B.desc} checks a handset.
b3: {B.desc} gets {A} to the door. Both go in, the door sliding shut.
{A} and {B.desc} tumble in at the door.
{B.desc} half drags {A} through the entry.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "You owe me breakfast for this, friend."
Overheard: {A} says: "You're the best... I will pay... tomorrow."
